implementation_notes: The router object collapses into LINQ plus Task.WhenAll: the recipient set is an IEnumerable<Recipient> resolved per message, and one await Task.WhenAll(recipients.Select(r => r.SendAsync(copy, ct))) performs the traversal and signals completion of the whole fan-out. Message brokers on .NET (MassTransit, NServiceBus) supply Send/Publish primitives and transport policies, but the computed-recipient loop itself stays application code, so the framework does not replace this pattern. Hand-written router classes remain justified when the recipient source, the per-recipient error policy and the concurrency limit must all be configurable components rather than inline LINQ.
pitfalls: Task.WhenAll surfaces only the first exception on await; the other recipients' failures are visible solely through the returned task's Exception.InnerExceptions, so swallow-by-await loses them.
Projecting a lazily-evaluated recipient source into tasks enumerates it while sends are already in flight; materialise the list first (ToList) if the source is not thread-safe.
An unbounded WhenAll over a large recipient list can exhaust the thread pool and outbound connections; Parallel.ForEachAsync or a SemaphoreSlim bounds the concurrency.
